title: 1972 AHSME Problem 13
statement: Inside square \(ABCD\) with sides of length \(12\) inches, segment \(AE\) is drawn, where \(E\) is the point on \(DC\) which is \(5\) inches from \(D.\) The perpendicular bisector of \(AE\) is drawn and intersects \(AE,\) \(AD,\) and \(BC\) at points \(M,\) \(P,\) and \(Q,\) respectively. The ratio of segment \(PM\) to \(MQ\) is:

solutions.text:
Because \(M\) is the midpoint of \(AE,\) its horizontal distance from \(AD\) is \(\frac{5}{2}.\) Its distance from \(BC\) is \[ 12-\frac52=\frac{19}{2}. \] The two right triangles cut from line \(PQ\) by the horizontal through \(M\) are similar, so their hypotenuses are in the ratio of these horizontal legs: \[ PM:MQ=\frac52:\frac{19}{2}=5:19. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Draw through \(M\) a line parallel to \(AB\)
The horizontal distances from \(M\) to \(AD\) and \(BC\) are \(\frac{5}{2}\) and \(\frac{19}{2}\)
